DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City JAN 25 vvvwv.dilg.gov.ph Orr-G OPINION NO. S. MR. ROLANDO T. AGLIBOT City Treasurer, City of Alaminos, Pangasinan Alaminos City Hall Quezon Avenue, City of Alaminos Pangasinan Dear Mr. Aglibot: This pertains to your letter dated May IO, 2023 requesting for the Department's opinion on the propriety for the National Food Authority (NFA) to pay real property tax (RPT) in favor of the City Government of Alaminos. Per your letter, the City Government of Alaminos, Pangasinan issued a statement of account to the NFA demanding payment of RPT in the amount of Php 1,128,876.60. However, NFA maintains that it is a government instrumentality exempt from payment of RPT). Hence, the request for clarification on the following specific queries: 1. Whether the National Food Authority is a Government-Owned and Controlled Corporation or a Government Instrumentality? 2. Whether the National Food Authority is indeed exempt from Real Property Tax? We provide a single discussion in response to the queries presented which appeared to be interrelated. In the March 16, 2022 Decision of the Court of Tax Appeals on National Food Authority (NFA) vs. Malolos Bulacanl, the NFA was classified as a government instrumentality based on its scrutiny of P.D. No. 4 as amended by PD No. 1485 and P.D. No. 1770 and R.A. No. 11203, vis-å-vis the pronouncements in MIAA vs. Court of Appeals2. It is an instrumentality of the government performing as it does "essential public services for the common good, services that every modern State must provide its citizens". In the same case, NFA was determined exempt from Real Property Tax pursuant to Section 6 of P.D. No. 4, as amended, viz: Sec. 6. Administration — Powers, Organization, Management and Exemptions. — The powers, organization, management and exemptions of the Authority shall be as follows: (d) Exemptions. — in furtherance to the effective implementation of the policy enunciated in this decree, the Authority is hereby declared exempt: I CTA AC No. 241; March 16, 2022 2 G.R. No. 155650; July 20, 2006 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline Nov: 8876-34-54

From payment of all taxes, duties, fees, imposts, charges, costs and restrictions to the Republic of the Philippines, its provinces, cities, municipalities, ...xxx..." (Emphasis Supplied) The Decision expounded on this as hereinbelow cited: Considering the clear and categorical provisions of Sections 133 (o) and 234 of the LGC, the act of respondents in demanding payment of RPT from petitioner is ultra vires. Respondents were bereft of any power or authority to assess and collect RPT from petitioner, more so, there being nothing on record to show that beneficial use of the subject property has been granted to a taxable person. Consequently, the two (2) Notices of Realty Tax Delinquency issued against petitioner are void ab initio and collection of the amount therein thereof may not be justified. Like a void judgment, a void assessment produces no legal effect; it never attains finality and — akin to an outlaw — it may be slain whenever or wherever it exhibits its head. While it may be true that the cited case is still with the CTA, you may use the rationale and justification cited by the court to guide you in your next course of action. The foregoing legal opinion is being rendered based on the facts as herein narrated, without prejudice to the contrary decisions hereinafter rendered by a competent court or stand issued by a competent body.
